hints.title: Co-purchased Item Pairing
hints.text: Link purchase entries sharing the same buyer to detect products bought together.

hints.title: Strict Index Ordering
hints.text: Enforce a strict inequality between product identifiers to prevent duplicate mirrored pairs.

hints.title: Aggregation and Threshold Filtering
hints.text: Group by both products and their respective categories, retaining pairs with at least three distinct buyers.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
SELECT 
    P1.product_id AS product1_id, 
    P2.product_id AS product2_id, 
    PI1.category AS product1_category, 
    PI2.category AS product2_category, 
    COUNT(DISTINCT P1.user_id) AS customer_count 
FROM ProductPurchases AS P1 
INNER JOIN ProductPurchases AS P2 
    ON P1.user_id = P2.user_id AND P1.product_id < P2.product_id 
LEFT JOIN ProductInfo AS PI1 
    ON P1.product_id = PI1.product_id 
LEFT JOIN ProductInfo AS PI2 
    ON P2.product_id = PI2.product_id 
GROUP BY P1.product_id, P2.product_id, PI1.category, PI2.category 
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT P1.user_id) >= 3 
ORDER BY customer_count DESC, product1_id ASC, product2_id ASC;
```

variables: N: number of purchase records in ProductPurchases
complexity.notes: Self-joining purchase records on identical customer identifiers generates candidate pairs.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Without ordering constraints on product pairs, redundant duplicates and self-pairs pollute the result.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Grouping by product pairs collapses individual transactions into aggregated counts.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use inner self-joins with inequality filters and aggregate having conditions.
